# graphwalk

> Fast, probabilistic question answering over an existing knowledge graph. Each hop is a constrained classification decision made by a fast model (Jev), so a walk's answer comes with a confidence; low-confidence walks can be escalated to an LLM decider. Python library, CLI, and MCP server.

When to use it, measured: graphwalk wins on large or messy graph schemas (3–5x the F1 of LLM-written queries, at 1/20 the cost), and its confidence separates right from wrong answers (AUROC up to 0.97), so walks can escalate to an LLM decider only when unsure (its accuracy at about half its cost on MetaQA, though an LLM-written query was cheaper still there). It is the wrong tool for QA over documents (multi-step RAG wins by 10–19 F1), for small clean schemas (an LLM writing the query is more accurate), and for questions with constraints or superlatives. The installed package carries the same guide: run `graphwalk guide`.
